task.title: Course catalogue
task.html:
JLearn courses

Loading...
task.description: The page has an empty list #course-list and a paragraph #course-count. The platform sets an array courses of objects { id, title, lessons, isNew }. Write a function renderCourses(list): clear #course-list; for every course create an li with the class course, the text "HTML - 10 lessons" and data-id from id; add the class course--new to courses with isNew: true; write "Courses: N" into #course-count from the array length. At the end call renderCourses(courses). Do not use innerHTML or element.style.

tests.name: The page has 3 li.course elements
tests.fail: For every course create an li, add the class course and insert it into #course-list with append.

tests.name: The class course--new only on JavaScript
Calling it again does not double the list
tests.check: (() => { renderCourses([{ id: "py", title: "Python", lessons: 12, isNew: false }]); return document.querySelectorAll("#course-list li.course").length === 1 && document.querySelectorAll("#course-list li.course")[0].textContent === "Python - 12 lessons" && document.querySelector("#course-count").textContent === "Courses: 1"; })()
tests.fail: Clear the list before rendering: container.textContent = ""; and use the list parameter.

tests.name: Empty array: the list is empty, "Courses: 0"
tests.fail: With an empty array the loop does not run - but the clearing and the counter must still work.

tests.name: Text is output as text, not markup
tests.check: (() => { renderCourses([{ id: "x", title: "Hack", lessons: 1, isNew: false }]); const li = document.querySelectorAll("#course-list li.course")[0]; return li.textContent === "Hack - 1 lessons" && li.querySelector("b") === null; })()

tests.name: Elements are created with createElement and append
The program runs without errors
tests.fail: A null error - check the selectors: #course-list, #course-count.

wrong_solutions.mistake: the counter is a fixed number

questions.question: What is the DOM?
options: The tree of objects the browser builds from HTML
questions.explanation: JavaScript changes the DOM; the file stays the same.

questions.question: Match the code with what it finds.
pairs: The first element with the class card
questions.explanation: The selectors are the same as in CSS.

questions.question: What does document.querySelector(".nope") return if there is no such element?
questions.explanation: querySelector returns null; accessing its properties gives a TypeError.

questions.question: Why is text from user data output with textContent and not innerHTML?
options: innerHTML runs the markup and someone else's code from the string (XSS)
innerHTML does not work in Chrome
questions.explanation: textContent shows the text as it is.

questions.question: Which methods does classList have?
questions.explanation: classList manages classes, and CSS defines the styling.

questions.question: card.classList.toggle("active") was called twice. Is the active class there if it was not there at first?
options: There will be two active classes
questions.explanation: The first call adds it, the second removes it.

questions.question: How do you read the data-lessons attribute of the element el? Type the expression.
questions.explanation: dataset holds all data attributes; the value is always a string.

questions.question: Why is appearance changed with classList and not element.style?
options: Styles stay in CSS: they can be overridden, adapted and found
questions.explanation: element.style writes to the style="" attribute - which we gave up in the CSS course.

questions.question: Steps of creating an element: match the step with the code.
questions.explanation: Without append the element exists only in memory.

questions.question: Why does renderCourses clear the list before rendering?
options: So that calling it again does not double the elements
questions.explanation: Render rebuilds the list from the current data.

questions.question: Which element property hides it from screen readers too? Type the property name.
Why might the error "Cannot set properties of null" appear?
options: A script without defer ran before the HTML was parsed
The element does not exist on this page
questions.explanation: In all three cases querySelector returned null.
